I'll take TCU Horned Frogs +14.5, down to +12.5 . The Red Raiders opened as 10.5-point favorites at Kalshi. However, the line movement feels driven more by perception than new information . TCU firing Sonny Dykes this week is a new development, but Texas Tech's statistical edge and the Horned Frogs' absence of starting quarterback Jaden Craig were already factored into the opening line . More importantly, the Red Raiders rank 77th nationally in third-down conversion rate and 108th in red-zone scoring rate . That's a problem when laying nearly two touchdowns because converting in high-leverage situations is how favorites build a margin. TCU vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 47.5 The Under 47.5 is tradable down to 45.5 . Texas Tech can overwhelm TCU, so the Horned Frogs need to turn this game into a rock fight to have any shot at an upset. The Red Raiders have the 16th-highest rushing rate in the country, and TCU's defense ranks 18th in yards per rush allowed . The Horned Frogs also have the third-best red-zone defense nationally, which could compound Texas Tech's struggles in high-leverage situations and force the Red Raiders to settle for field goals. Meanwhile, both offensive lines struggle with pass protection and both defenses have high sack rates, opening the door for drive-killing sacks. TCU vs Texas Tech combo I'm essentially investing in Texas Tech winning ugly, which wouldn't be the worst outcome for a team with legitimate College Football Playoff hopes. If TCU can avoid giving the Red Raiders short fields, Texas Tech might have to chew up a significant amount of clock to build a comfortable lead. Furthermore, a two-score deficit wouldn't necessarily force the Horned Frogs to abandon their offensive game plan early, especially if their defense is keeping them within striking distance. Tech couple Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The regular season comes to an end in Galaxy Stadium for the Texas Tech football team , with TCU coming to town for a Thanksgiving showdown under the lights. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. Texas Tech's J'Koby Williams runs with the ball against Arizona State during a Big 12 Conference football game, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. The fired coach theory and TCU TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Of those four other teams switching coaches in season, three of them won their next game, two of them (Baylor and NC State) earning wins of 21 points or more. This theory doesn't always come to fruition, however. During the 2025 coaching cycle, six power-conference programs fired coaches during the season and just one of them won their next game following the axing. That one win came from Virginia Tech, which beat Wofford, so it barely counts. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs TCU Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. away.headline: Backup QB likely to earn first start for TCU vs. No. 2 Utah after injury update
away.blurb: Senior quarterback Jaden Craig was initially expected to start and was listed as probable in the first Big 12 player availability report on Wednesday night. TCU head coach Sonny Dykes also said Tuesday that he believed Craig would be able to play. But Craig was downgraded to doubtful in Friday’s injury report and seems unlikely to play against the Utes. Craig was hobbled with an ankle injury during TCU’s 20-10 win over Kanas State last Saturday. Saturday night might mark the start of the Adam Schobel era for TCU football. The sophomore quarterback is expected to earn his first start when the Horned Frogs (5-5, 3-4) host No. 2 Utah (10-0, 7-0) at 8 p.m. Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium on Fox. “I would expect him to play, I think he was a lot better today than he was yesterday,” Dykes said Tuesday. “I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess.” Schobel has played sparingly this season, with just one passing attempt and 11 yards on four carries. But the former four-star recruit is largely viewed as the quarterback of the future for the program. Schobel got his most extensive action of his career in the win over the Wildcats, mostly on designed quarterback runs, but will now be tasked to lead the Horned Frogs against the highest-ranked opponent to play in the Carter since No. 2 Texas in 1970. Starting quarterback Jaden Craig landed on Friday night's Big 12 availability report as doubtful, putting sophomore backup Adam Schobel in line to make his first career start, per ESPN's Pete Thamel. TCU listed Craig as probable earlier in the week before downgrading him Friday night. Losing Craig deals a major blow to a 5-5 Horned Frogs offense chasing bowl eligibility against an undefeated 10-0 Utah squad. The Harvard transfer ranks third in the Big 12 with 266.4 passing yards per game, completing 223 of 344 throws for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions while adding four rushing scores. Against Kansas State last Saturday, Craig went 20-for-34 for 225 yards and a touchdown without throwing a pick. Now, the spotlight shifts to Schobel. The 6-foot-5 former four-star recruit from Columbus, Texas, has seen limited action across three appearances this season. He threw one incomplete pass against the Grambling Tigers in September and logged four carries for 11 yards, including three rushes for three yards against Kansas State. TCU's injury woes extend beyond the quarterback room. The Horned Frogs also ruled out running back G'Ivori Graham and linebacker Keylan Abrams for Saturday's contest in Fort Worth, though defensive tackles Markis Deal and Ansel Din-Mbuh alongside edge rusher Cheta Ofili remain probable. Meanwhile, Utah ruled out safety Marcus Wimberly and listed long snapper Logan Castor as questionable. Throwing a first-time starter against the Big 12's top team is no easy task, but Schobel gets his shot to shock college football under the Fort Worth lights. away.blurb: Florida put out and official injury update on the star pass catcher Tuesday afternoon, saying that Brown has opted to undergo surgery on his injured knee. Per the statement, the procedure is expected to solve the lingering issue for good, but it will also keep him on the shelf for the “immediate future.” A 5-star recruit in the 2025 cycle, Brown became one of the biggest recruiting wins for the Gators in recent memory when he chose Florida over several other big name schools. He put together a solid freshman season under former head coach Billy Napier before breaking out during Florida's first 4 games of the 2026 campaign, becoming the primary target for quarterback Aaron Philo during that early stretch. He hauled in 17 catches for 271 yards and 2 touchdowns before suffering the aforementioned knee injury during the Gators' Week 4 win against Ole Miss, missing several weeks as a result. It initially looked like Brown would be able to return for Florida's matchup against Georgia , but he ended up reaggravating the injury during the bye week prolonged his absence. He'll be out this week. He's not going to play,” Sumrall said. “He's dying to play. It's an unfortunate deal.” “It was substantial enough that we knew it would put him on the shelf for a little while,” Sumrall said. “Maybe a week, two, three weeks, didn't really know. But felt like there would be a timetable to return that wouldn't be terribly long.” Brown continued to reappear on the injury report in the weeks that followed. Coming out of the bye week, Sumrall said, Brown “practiced really good on Monday and Tuesday” before reinjuring his knee in a non-contact incident during Wednesday practice in Week 9, forcing him to miss Florida's matchup against Georgia. Before the Gators' 34-27 win against Vanderbilt on Saturday, Sumrall appeared unsure about Brown's return to the field. “It's hurting him as much as anybody. He wants to play. He cares. He's a Gator,” Sumrall said. “Can't wait to watch him get back on the field. He makes everyone around him better. He's a quarterback's best friend. You get him the ball in space and he makes things happen. But he will not be available this week.” No. 3 Florida Holds Off Milwaukee in Return Home From Vegas Listen & Schedule Listen & Schedule The sophomore first appeared on the injury report after suffering a knee strain in the second quarter of Florida's Week 4 win against Ole Miss. I'm hopeful everybody can play,” he said at the time. How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As of Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Florida Gators officially shut down wide receiver Vernell Brown III for the rest of the season. This is news that came as no surprise , and it's crazy to see it take as long as it did. Brown had only suited up for four games this season, but he continued to appear on injury reports leading up to Florida's 34-27 win against Vanderbilt. The 7-4 Gators certainly could've used Brown in that brutal one-win stretch from Oct. 3 to Nov. 7, but at the end of the day they bounced back terrifically from Nov. 14 onward. Brown was a crucial part of this team's 4-0 start as he recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards with a pair of touchdowns. For reference, he's still third on the team in receiving yards, proving just how valuable he was during the few games when he was around. For the Gators, it's business as usual going into the final game of the year, a rivalry showdown at Florida State. Finally, Florida's offense knows it can move on once and for all without Brown. That's not a sentence they wanted to hear back on Sept. 26, but it's been a long time coming as his status had been in doubt for the better part of two months. Brown is only a sophomore, so the Gators risking further injury by putting him back on the field was never going to be the right answer. The Florida native made an immediate impact as a freshman with his 40 receptions for 512 yards. Obviously, this season took quite a turn with those losses to Missouri and South Carolina, and it doesn't feel like a coincidence that the offense scored fewer than 20 points in those games without Brown. Running back Jadan Baugh was not a factor in either of those games either, so that also didn't help the Gators chances when they lost their offensive superstar. When Brown and Baugh were both on the field, this team looked absolutely unstoppable. Now, it'll once again be up to Aaron Philo to keep this run-game going, though he looked much better through the air against the Commodores. Florida State enters this non-conference game at 5-6 overall, fighting for bowl eligibility against a Brown-less Gators offense.

home.blurb: However, Luke Fickell and Co. didn’t just leave SECU Stadium with a bruised ego, as newly-donned starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins was recently listed as questionable in Wisconsin’s latest injury availability report ahead of this weekend’s clash against the Purdue Boilermakers . The Wisconsin Badgers are stumbling to the end of the 2026 football season, as their 24-21 loss against the Maryland Terrapins last weekend did them no favors. What does this mean for Wisconsin’s quarterback situation? In Hopkins’ two starts for the Badgers , the Mater Dei product tallied 318 yards through the air, on a 63% completion rate, along with three touchdowns and two fumbles. In Wisconsin’s last-second loss to the Terps, Hopkins finished with just 55 yards in the air, continuing a trend of disappointing quarterback play in 2026. If Hopkins is unable to go, it's plausible that original starter Colton Joseph gets the start, as the former Old Dominion quarterback has totaled 1,739 all-purpose yards, along with 15 total touchdowns and six turnovers. For the 122nd time since 1897, Michigan and Ohio State will meet in a rivalry known as "The Game." Photo By - Reuters Connect. Charles Woodson (2) and Archie Griffin (45) are two key figures in the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry. Arguably the greatest rivalry in all of sports returns in Week 13 of the college football season, with Ohio State hosting Michigan at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio, at noon ET (FOX) on Saturday, Nov. 28. This year's edition of the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry , known simply as The Game, is different from recent years, with both programs enduring down seasons and neither contending for a national championship. Some would argue that makes this the purest version of the rivalry, with both teams fueled by their dislike for each other and little else. Ohio State is a 10.5-point favorite, and my college football picks back the Buckeyes to win big. Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry history: The Game Wins (official; six ties) 9 (1901-1909) Longest win streak 8 (2012-2019) Largest margin of victory 1027-367-36 (.731) Program record 997-342-53 (.735) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks Few rivalries feature two teams as successful as Michigan and Ohio State . That history makes their mutual hatred even more intense. The Wolverines and the Buckeyes have both won plenty of national championships, produced multiple Heisman Trophy winners, and sent countless players to the NFL, but more than anything else, they take pride in beating each other. This rivalry is built as much on program success as it is on animosity. Michigan has more wins than any other program in college football history, and Ohio State has a higher winning percentage than any other program in college football history. The Game often has major implications for the national championship and the Heisman Trophy race. It all began in 1897, and The Game has been played every season since 1918, except in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Its history stretches from Fielding Yost's early dominance through Woody Hayes and Bo Schembechler's Ten-Year War, Jim Tressel and Urban Meyer's successful runs, and Jim Harbaugh's revival of Michigan. This is the college football rivalry. Recent Michigan-Ohio State results Nov. 29, 2025 27-9 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-9.5) Nov. 30, 2024 13-10 (Michigan) Michigan (+19.5) Nov. 25, 2023 30-24 (Michigan) Michigan (-3.5) Nov. 26, 2022 45-23 (Michigan) Michigan (+8.5) Nov. 27, 2021 42-27 (Michigan) Michigan (+7) Nov. 30, 2019 56-27 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-9) Nov. 24, 2018 62-39 (Ohio State) Ohio State (+3.5) Nov. 25, 2017 31-20 (Ohio State) Michigan (+12.5) Nov. 26, 2016 30-27 (Ohio State) Michigan (+4.5) Nov. 28, 2015 42-13 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-1.5) History of the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry When did the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry start? The Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry began in 1897 and was immediately a natural rivalry because of the bordering states' history with the Toledo War (a boundary dispute between the states over the Toledo Strip). The Wolverines won the first matchup on Oct. 16, 1897, in Ann Arbor, 34-0. The programs didn't meet again until a 0-0 tie in 1900, then played every season through 1912. Michigan went 12-0-2 against Ohio State from 1897 to 1912. The Buckeyes didn't win The Game for the first time until 1919, beating Michigan 13-3 to spark a three-game winning streak. However, Michigan owned the rivalry, for the most part, until Hayes arrived in 1951. The Wolverines went 32-12-4 against Ohio State from 1897 to 1950. Why is it called The Game? Michigan vs. Ohio State is known to most as The Game because of its importance to both fan bases and college football nationally. The matchup has closed out the regular season since 1935, and usually there's plenty on the line when these teams meet. Before Big Ten expansion, the winner of The Game would frequently win the conference and head to the Rose Bowl for a chance at a national title. And in later years, The Game would play a key role in setting the Big Ten Championship Game matchup. The loser of The Game generally considers the season a disappointment. What was the Ten-Year War? What kicked off the Ten-Year War between Michigan and Ohio State was the Wolverines hiring Hayes' protege, Schembechler, in 1969. Schembechler had been an assistant under Hayes at Ohio State from 1958 to 1962 before following in Hayes' footsteps and becoming head coach at Miami (OH). Both Hayes (1949-1950) and Schembechler (1963-1968) coached at Miami (Ohio) before taking over Ohio State and Michigan. Hayes went 12-6 against Michigan in The Game from 1951-1968 and flipped the once maize and blue-dominated rivalry to the scarlet and grey. That led Michigan in a new direction with the hiring of Schembechler, who immediately made his presence felt. In Schembechler's first game against Ohio State, Michigan pulled off "the upset of the century" by beating the No. 1 Buckeyes 24-12 and ending their 22-game winning streak. That victory marked the beginning of the Ten-Year War. From 1970 to 1975, in four of the six meetings, both Ohio State and Michigan were ranked in the top five. During the Ten-Year War, the programs shared the Big Ten title multiple times, with Michigan ultimately having the upper hand, going 5-4-1 against Ohio State. The war ended after the 1978 season, when Hayes was fired for punching Clemson linebacker Charlie Bauman after an interception in the Gator Bowl. It was during the Ten-Year War that Ohio State began its tradition of referring to Michigan as "That Team Up North" when Hayes referred to the Wolverines as such. Best moments in the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry The Snow Bowl (1950) Among the most famous games in the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry, the Snow Bowl was exactly what it sounds like: a game in a blizzard. The blizzard was so bad that the Buckeyes were given the option to cancel the game (they would have won the Big Ten title by default if they had), but Ohio State wanted to play its rival. All in all, the teams combined to punt the ball 45 times, with many of the punts coming on first down as they battled for field position and hoped the other team would fumble. Michigan would block two punts, one resulting in a safety and the other a touchdown, to win 9-3. The Wolverines didn't complete a single pass or gain a single first down, but took home the Big Ten title with the win. Ohio State head coach Wes Fesler would resign after the loss, leading to Hayes being hired. The Upset of the Century (1969) In Schembechler's first game against his former boss, Michigan would upset undefeated No. 1-ranked Ohio State 24-12. The Buckeyes were riding a 22-game winning streak and gunning for their second straight national title, but an all-time performance from Barry Pierson (three interceptions and a 60-yard punt return that set up a touchdown) would end Ohio State's shot at a championship. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty Ohio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey after losing his last two games Getty It's been a rough month for the Ohio State Buckeyes. Ohio State started 6-1 but has lost three of its last four games. The latest was Saturday's 31-28 loss at Nebraska, which officially knocked the Buckeyes out of the College Football Playoff race. All that's left now is "The Game" against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday in Columbus. On paper, Ohio State has the better roster. Even former Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer admits that. Meyer, who went 7-0 against Michigan during his time in Columbus, still picked Ohio State to win. However, it sounds like he wouldn't be all that surprised if Michigan ended up leaving Columbus with a win. Urban Meyer's 1 Major Michigan Concern GettyMichigan and Ohio State both head into the Big Game with serious question marks Meyer spoke on stage at an event in a video posted Sunday by 10TV Sports' Adam King, and he didn't sugarcoat where Ohio State stands. "The roster's better — Ohio State — but the best unit performing right now is the Wolverine defense. And that concerns me a little bit," Meyer said . "They really hammered UCLA. You got to think, the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible — they're last in the country. And so, to still have decent numbers — only one team has over 21 points on them all year, and that was Oregon — that's a legit defense. "On offense, we got the best player in the country, maybe the best player to ever play college football — that's how good Jeremiah is. But we also have a backup quarterback, and the offensive line is not playing great. So, I think this is going to be a rock fight; a low-scoring game, and I think whoever punches the hardest is going to win the game. I expect it to be a 17-10, 17-14 game and I got the Buckeyes." The numbers back up Meyer's remarks. Michigan ranks 17th nationally in scoring defense (17.5 points per game) and ninth in total defense (278.3 yards per game). And Oregon, which beat Michigan 31-7, is the only team to score more than 21 points on the Wolverines all season. The Wolverines' defense was at its best last Saturday in an 18-16 triple-overtime upset of previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA. Michigan held the Bruins to 187 yards through three quarters and finished with three forced turnovers and four sacks. Why Urban Meyer Expects a Rock Fight vs. Michigan GettyOhio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey The biggest reason for Meyer's worry is at quarterback. Starter Julian Sayin hurt his right (throwing) arm in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17, and he isn't expected back for Michigan. That leaves true freshman Luke Fahey under center. Fahey went 16 of 27 for 259 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception at Nebraska. But nearly all of that came early: He was 9 of 12 for 163 yards and two scores in the first half, then 7 of 15 for 96 yards after halftime. Jeremiah Smith did his part (six catches, 165 yards, two touchdowns), tying Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record with 17 receiving TDs. Meyer also didn't pull any punches when it came to the other side of the ball for Michigan. "That defense is legit, legit because that offense is pathetic up there. It's the worst offense in college football, yet they're in almost all the games," Meyer said . "Their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal. Our defense has been up-and-down a little bit, but their offense stinks. I see this being a very low-scoring game. This is Ohio State-Wolverine football. The toughest team is going to win this game." Michigan's offense isn't quite the worst in the country, but it's close. The Wolverines rank 131st nationally in scoring (18.3 points per game). It's quite a shift for Meyer, who reportedly called the 2026 Wolverines a "train wreck" in early October. The Buckeyes (7-4) and Wolverines (6-5) kick off at noon ET Saturday at Ohio Stadium on Fox. Thornton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Wed, November 25, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The final week of what has been a disappointing regular season has arrived, as the Michigan Wolverines are hitting the road to take on the Ohio State Buckeyes in The Game. A few weeks ago, this was a day that Michigan fans were dreading, but the Wolverines are actually coming into this one with more momentum than the Buckeyes. Michigan fans finally had reason to celebrate last week, as the Wolverines knocked off previously undefeated UCLA in the Big House in triple overtime. After a difficult first ten games, senior day in Ann Arbor was a resounding success. On the other side, Ohio State is having its worst season in nearly 15 years. The Buckeyes are currently 7-4 after losing three of their last four games, and last week was an unfortunate one, as Ohio State became the first ranked team to lose to Nebraska since 2016. All in all, it has been a long time since The Game featured two teams struggling like this. The season is over for both teams, but still, it's The Game. It's going to be a battle, and here are a few bold predictions for the matchup: Savion Hiter will rush for over 150 yards Yes, you read that right. For the first time in weeks, I am making a positive prediction for the Wolverines. When they go up against a team coached by Ryan Day, anything is possible. The winner of The Game has won the rushing battle every single year for the last 24 years. If Michigan has a good day on the ground, there is a solid chance that it can pull off the upset. Savion Hiter has rushed for over 100 yards in each of Michigan's last two games, so he is playing his best ball at the right time. Last week, the Buckeyes gave up 176 rushing yards to Nebraska, and Ohio State only gained 76 yards. With Michigan's lack of a passing game, the run game needs to have a good day. Michigan will win on the last play of the game One thing about this Michigan team is it has a flair for the dramatic. In 11 games, three have ended with a score on the final play of the game to win the game. Of the other eight, six have been one-score games. There's a solid chance that this is going to be another close one. There have already been three games that ended with a score on the final play, so why not one more? I think this is going to be another close one between these two bitter rivals, and Michigan will win in dramatic fashion one more time. Michigan wins 17-13 In rivalry games like this, you can forget about what has happened leading up to this contest. A big reason why I picked Michigan State to beat Michigan is that I knew that the Spartans would show up and play their best game of the year. They always do against Michigan. While I still don't think Kyle Whittingham can get his team up for a rivalry game like he should be able to, I do think that Ryan Day is in a particularly fragile state right now given the season that Ohio State has had and the current state of that program. Day seems to let the pressure get to him, and after the UCLA game, I feel like Michigan is playing with a "nothing to lose" mentality. Because of that, I have the Wolverines squeaking out a 17-13 victory.

Wolverines Football Updated: Nov. 24, 2026, 9:28 a.m. | Published: Nov. 23, 2026, 11:55 a.m. Aaron McMann | amcmann@mlive.com ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Kyle Whittingham said Monday morning that Michigan football would be sticking with Bryce Underwood at quarterback this week. Given what happened over the weekend, the Wolverines’ upset win over No. 4 UCLA, 18-16, in overtime, it makes sense. The sophomore didn’t put up impressive numbers, but did enough to help the team -- and completed the game-winning two-point conversion throw. “Bryce is the guy,” Whittingham told reporters ahead of Saturday’s rivalry showdown at Ohio State (12 p.m., FOX). “Bryce is the guy and Tommy (Carr) is the No. 2.” Whittingham did add a stipulator, calling it the plan “barring any(thing) unforeseen” like “getting dinged up in practice or something like that. “That’s how it will be,” Whittingham continued. Roughly 45 minutes later, CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reported that Underwood suffered a lower-body injury in the win over UCLA that left his status in question for Saturday’s game. Soon after, national reporters from On3 and ESPN confirmed the injury to Underwood. The quarterback appeared fine physically as he spoke to the press after the game on Saturday, calling it “a blessing” to get a second chance at being the Wolverines’ starting quarterback. Michigan will be required to submit a player availability report to the Big Ten beginning on Wednesday, with updates expected daily leading up to Saturday’s game in Columbus. RELATED: Michigan football a double-digit underdog vs. Ohio State In seven starts this season, Underwood has completed 54 percent of his throws for 1,077 yards and six touchdowns, with six interceptions and two fumbles lost. away.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood dealing with injury heading into Ohio State game
away.blurb: At his press conference on Monday morning, Michigan head football coach Kyle Whittingham said that sophomore Bryce Underwood is set to start in The Game this weekend against Ohio State. However, we’ll see if he’s able to even play at all. Per 247Sports’ Matt Zenitz, Underwood is dealing with a lower-body injury that he suffered during Saturday’s stunning upset win over UCLA. His status is “in question” heading into The Game in Columbus this weekend. Underwood has had quite the roller coaster season. He started the first six games of the season before freshman Tommy Carr took over after halftime of the Penn State game. Carr was then benched two weeks ago during the game at Oregon, and Underwood has taken every snap since. Despite the injury, Whittingham told the media on Monday morning that Underwood is “the guy” at quarterback, and that “barring anything unforeseen, getting dinged up in practice or something like that,” he will start against the Buckeyes on Saturday. Underwood completed just 11-of-24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown on Saturday vs UCLA. He also ran 13 times for five yards, losing one fumble in the process. On the season, he has completed 85-of-156 passes (54.5 percent) for 1,077 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions, while also running 76 times for 230 yards and an additional two scores. Should Underwood not be able to play in this one, Carr will be the next man up for the Wolverines. The true freshman has completed 67-of-106 passes this season for 686 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s also ran 49 times for 138 yards and three touchdowns. Wolverines Football Updated: Nov. 24, 2026, 9:28 a.m. | Published: Nov. 23, 2026, 11:55 a.m. Aaron McMann | amcmann@mlive.com ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Kyle Whittingham said Monday morning that Michigan football would be sticking with Bryce Underwood at quarterback this week. Given what happened over the weekend, the Wolverines’ upset win over No. 4 UCLA, 18-16, in overtime, it makes sense. The sophomore didn’t put up impressive numbers, but did enough to help the team -- and completed the game-winning two-point conversion throw. “Bryce is the guy,” Whittingham told reporters ahead of Saturday’s rivalry showdown at Ohio State (12 p.m., FOX). “Bryce is the guy and Tommy (Carr) is the No. 2.” Whittingham did add a stipulator, calling it the plan “barring any(thing) unforeseen” like “getting dinged up in practice or something like that. “That’s how it will be,” Whittingham continued. Roughly 45 minutes later, CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reported that Underwood suffered a lower-body injury in the win over UCLA that left his status in question for Saturday’s game. Soon after, national reporters from On3 and ESPN confirmed the injury to Underwood. The quarterback appeared fine physically as he spoke to the press after the game on Saturday, calling it “a blessing” to get a second chance at being the Wolverines’ starting quarterback. Michigan will be required to submit a player availability report to the Big Ten beginning on Wednesday, with updates expected daily leading up to Saturday’s game in Columbus. RELATED: Michigan football a double-digit underdog vs. Ohio State In seven starts this season, Underwood has completed 54 percent of his throws for 1,077 yards and six touchdowns, with six interceptions and two fumbles lost. Turnovers got him benched during a Week 6 win over Penn State, opening the door for freshman Tommy Carr to take over.

home.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood dealing with injury heading into Ohio State game
home.blurb: At his press conference on Monday morning, Michigan head football coach Kyle Whittingham said that sophomore Bryce Underwood is set to start in The Game this weekend against Ohio State. However, we’ll see if he’s able to even play at all. Per 247Sports’ Matt Zenitz, Underwood is dealing with a lower-body injury that he suffered during Saturday’s stunning upset win over UCLA. His status is “in question” heading into The Game in Columbus this weekend. Underwood has had quite the roller coaster season. He started the first six games of the season before freshman Tommy Carr took over after halftime of the Penn State game. Carr was then benched two weeks ago during the game at Oregon, and Underwood has taken every snap since. Despite the injury, Whittingham told the media on Monday morning that Underwood is “the guy” at quarterback, and that “barring anything unforeseen, getting dinged up in practice or something like that,” he will start against the Buckeyes on Saturday. Underwood completed just 11-of-24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown on Saturday vs UCLA. He also ran 13 times for five yards, losing one fumble in the process. On the season, he has completed 85-of-156 passes (54.5 percent) for 1,077 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions, while also running 76 times for 230 yards and an additional two scores. Should Underwood not be able to play in this one, Carr will be the next man up for the Wolverines. The true freshman has completed 67-of-106 passes this season for 686 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s also ran 49 times for 138 yards and three touchdowns. Michigan vs Ohio State is set for a noon kickoff on FOX.

home.blurb: Ohio State football plays rival Michigan on Nov. 28 in a game without College Football Playoff stakes attached to either team. Michigan is 6-5 under first-year coach Kyle Whittingham . Both teams have had their fair share of trouble at the quarterback position. Ohio State lost Julian Sayin due to injury in the Ohio State-Indiana game and has used freshman Luke Fahey the last four games. Michigan has swapped back and forth between quarterbacks Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr and ranks 132nd in the FBS in yards per game. Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is still the favorite for the Heisman trophy despite Ohio State's woes. Smith leads college football in receiving yards and touchdowns this season and is coming off a two-touchdown performance against Nebraska. Though Smith had a successful day, Ohio State struggled defensively in its 31-28 loss to Nebraska Nov. 21. The Buckeyes gave up 124 yards of offense in the first quarter, which is the most it allowed in the opening 15 minutes this season. The Buckeyes announced Tuesday that Smith will serve as the honorary victory bell ringer before Saturday’s matchup with the Wolverines. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. How to watch Louisville Cardinals vs. Kentucky Wildcats Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 12:00 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a +2.5-point underdog after the Wildcats were previously -1.5-point favorites. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 35.6% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction: Before the season started, I predicted Kentucky would win six games but lose to Louisville, believing Will Stein would have too much emotion coaching against his former team, where he once played. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Although this year’s game will be played at Kroger Field, I believe the Wildcats will pull off another victory in a high-scoring contest. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. picks.headline: Clemson Given Lackluster Prediction Ahead of South Carolina Showdown
picks.blurb: Clemson Given Lackluster Prediction Ahead of South Carolina Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NCAAF Scores / Schedule Clemson Given Lackluster Prediction Ahead of South Carolina Showdown (Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports - Clemson Tue, November 24, 2026 at 11:55 p.m. UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads About our Ads The Clemson Tigers were able to take down the Duke Blue Devils on the road last week, picking up a massive win for the season. Clemson is now 7-4 on the season, with the team having won four of its last six games overall. The Tigers have rebounded nicely from a poor opening part of the season, despite a lackluster offense all year. But as the Tigers prepare for the final week of the regular season, the only focus is on getting a win over the rival South Carolina Gamecocks. Clemson will be hosting South Carolina in the game, giving themselves a slight edge entering the contest. South Carolina will come into the game with a record of 6-5 for the season, coming off two straight blow out losses. The Gamecocks have lost by a score of 34-6 in two straight weeks, and they will try to bounce back this week against Clemson. Both sides understand the rivalry aspect of this game, with the Tigers wanting to add another win to the season's resume. But South Carolina won't go down quietly, looking to spoil the Tigers' final home game of the year. Heading into the game, the Tigers are being viewed as the underdogs, despite having the better record than South Carolina. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson has a 44.2 percent chance of taking down the Gamecocks this week at home. Quarterback Trent Pearman will likely get the starting nod in this game after leading the Tigers to a win last week. Pearman did well enough for Clemson to win, and it seems that the program wants to see more from him in this game. Overall, Pearman went 17-of-27 for 164 yards, with no touchdown passes against the Blue Devils. But he did rush for 51 yards and a touchdown, showing that he can be a dual-threat option for Clemson. If Pearman can continue to help the offense, it could give Clemson an opportunity to grab the win. Clemson's defense has been strong all year, and South Carolina's offense has been very stagnant over the last few weeks. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney has been criticized all season long , but if this team could get a win over the Gamecocks, it could go a long way for him. The 2026 season won't be seen as a complete success, but after how it started, the Tigers may end the year on a high note.

Tech couple Former Clemson football safety Khalil Barnes picks off South Carolina Drew Landon, Clemson Wire · Clemson Wire Sun, November 22, 2026 at 3:24 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Khalil Barnes may have traded orange for red and black, but habits from longtime friends are hard to get rid of. The former Clemson football player came down with a late third-quarter interception against rivals South Carolina on Saturday night, ending a Gamecocks red-zone threat and helping top-ranked Georgia hold a 27-6 lead going into the fourth quarter. South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was driving inside the Georgia 22 when he forced a throw into traffic. Barnes was lingering and waiting. The pick took away South Carolina's best chance to cut into the deficit and handed the ball straight back to the Bulldogs. It was the only turnover of the night for either team at that point and the only one South Carolina couldn't afford at the time. The Gamecocks, ranked 21st at 6-4, had managed just two field goals before the interception. Georgia, 9-1 and ranked first, had already built a two-score cushion behind two Nate Frazier rushing touchdowns and a pair of field goals from Peyton Woodring. For Clemson fans, the sight of Barnes snuffing out a South Carolina drive had to feel familiar probably even a tad bit confusing for the head to digest. He left Death Valley, but nobody let his instincts know that they should do the same. Somewhere in Upstate South Carolina, Tigers fans are watching a former player in a Bulldogs jersey do exactly what they would have asked of him, and deciding whether to be proud or just slightly annoyed that it's happening in another uniform. Barnes may be wearing a Georgia G now, but the Tiger paw is clearly still stamped somewhere in his blood. The Gamecocks will need to regroup quickly if they are to win this one. Georgia leads 27-6 with the fourth quarter just starting up. This was written in the fourth quarter of the Georgia vs. South Carolina game. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) Getty Zach Lentz · HEAVY Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:52 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads CLEMSON, S.C. — The Palmetto Bowl returns to Death Valley on Saturday with pride, momentum, and a surprising betting line on the table. Despite boasting a better record and home-field advantage, the Clemson Tigers (7-4) are once again playing the underdog role. FanDuel oddsmakers have installed the South Carolina Gamecocks (6-5) as 5.5-point road favorites for the regular-season finale. The Gamecocks sit at -215 on the moneyline, while the Tigers offer +180 value. The over/under is set at a gritty 41.5 points. For the second consecutive year, both programs enter the rivalry unranked in the US LBM Coaches Poll, though Clemson quietly garnered 11 votes on Sunday. But national rankings rarely dictate the tempo of this bitter in-state clash. Clemson's Ground Game and Stifling Defense Clemson enters Saturday riding the high of a defensive masterclass. Just days ago, the Tigers walked into Durham as 13.5-point underdogs and dismantled Duke 20-10. The blueprint was simple: control the clock and suffocate the opposition. Clemson's defense allowed just 11 first downs all night, keeping the Blue Devils' offense on the field for a paltry 22 minutes and 45 seconds. By the time Duke regained possession following Chris Denson's 7-yard, fourth-quarter touchdown run, the game was effectively out of reach. Offensively, the Tigers unleashed a punishing, multi-pronged rushing attack. Three different players eclipsed the 50-yard mark, led by Jarvis Green's 84 yards on 16 carries and Denson's 71 yards. The catalyst, however, was Trent Pearman. In his first career start, the quarterback proved poised under pressure. Pearman completed 17 of 27 passes for 164 yards and added 51 yards on the ground. His decisive 9-yard touchdown scramble in the third quarter gave Clemson a lead it never relinquished. Now, he faces a South Carolina defense desperate for a bounce-back performance. Gamecocks Look to Rebound After Georgia Mauling South Carolina arrives in Death Valley needing a win to match Clemson's 7-4 record, but they must first shake off the lingering effects of a brutal 34-6 home loss to No. 1 Georgia. The Gamecocks' primary objective will be jumpstarting quarterback LaNorris Sellers. The top-ranked Bulldogs terrorized Sellers in the pocket, sacking him three times and intercepting him once. He finished the afternoon with just 87 passing yards and 24 rushing yards. If South Carolina is to cover the 5.5-point spread in one of college football's most hostile environments, Sellers will need the time and space that Georgia strictly denied him. Kickoff from Memorial Stadium is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET Saturday on ESPN2. away.blurb: Teams have released their first injury reports for the week. The most glaring omission from the report is the name of LaNorris Sellers . After being listed as questionable last week, Sellers was unable to participate against the Arkansas Razorbacks, which led to a blowout 34-6 loss. Sellers’s presence is a non-negotiable if the Gamecocks want to pull off an upset against the number one ranked Georgia Bulldogs , who arguably have the best defensive unit in the country. The Bulldogs have limited some of the best quarterbacks and offenses in the conference to a standstill, but Sellers could be one of the toughest tests they face all season. Though Sellers will be back, injury issues still loom over the Gamecocks. Leading rusher Matt Fuller IV is out. Receivers Mazeo Bennett Jr. and Nyck Harbor are listed as questionable along with EDGE’s Dylan Stewart and Anthony Addison. DB Judge Collier is also listed as questionable. away.headline: South Carolina vs. Georgia: Kickoff time, TV channel, injury report, odds
away.blurb: WR Nitro Tuggle, DB Jalewis Soloman, WR Jayden Sellers, RB Matt Fuller, EDGE Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josiah Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. WR Mazeo Bennett, EDGE Dylan Stewart, DB Judge Collier, WR Nyck Harbor and EDGE Anthony Addison are all listed as questionable. All five of those players are starters at their respective positions and would be a massive loss should they not play this weekend. What’s going on at QB? There was confusion galore around South Carolina’s quarterback room last week. Is LaNorris Sellers healthy? Would he be available? Is he going to play? What’s the definition of probable? Does anything anyone says really mean anything? The answer to those questions was that Cutter Woods started at quarterback for South Carolina in its loss to Arkansas. USC offensive coordinator Kendal Briles said “all” of the Gamecock quarterbacks practiced on Wednesday. It remains to be seen if Sellers will return from the ankle injury he sustained vs. Texas A&M or if Woods will get the second start of his career. Is all CFP hope lost? South Carolina’s hopes of making the College Football Playoff seemed completely lost after it was upset on the road by Arkansas last week. After all, there’s no way a team with four losses who was just defeated by an unranked team would stick around in the CFP rankings…right? Wrong. South Carolina remained in the CFP Top 25 , only dropping from No. 17 to No. 21. The odds of making the playoff are very slim but should South Carolina find a way to win out by beating No. 1 Georgia and Clemson then there’s a world where its playoff odds may graduate to just slim . Shane Beamer and the No. 21 Gamecocks will face No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. The game will kick off at 7:30 p.m. and be televised nationally on ABC. South Carolina (6-4, 4-4 SEC) is coming off a loss to Arkansas last week. Meanwhile, Georgia (9-1, 7-1 SEC) is coming off a win over Missouri at home. Georgia leads the all-time series over South Carolina 55-19-2. The Bulldogs have won the last four games in the series, including the last matchup in 2023. South Carolina’s last win in the series came in upset fashion in 2019. The Gamecocks haven’t beat Georgia at home in Columbia since 2014. Here’s everything you need to know about Saturday’s game. This is the seventh time the show, which airs from 9 a.m. to noon, has come to Columbia.

Rivalry weekend is upon us, a chance to right wrongs and establish year-long bragging rights in the face of a hated opponent. Not only does this weekend's slate offer conference championship and College Football Playoff implications, but the teams out of the mix are playing for something sacred -- respect. And a few coaches are trying to keep their jobs, too. We've picked out 10 of the most important games for Week 13, beginning Thursday in Lubbock, Texas and taking us all the way to Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon on Saturday night. Season results : Brad Crawford (74-37 straight up, 51-59-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (79-32 straight up, 56–54-1 ATS) After matching winning weeks, at least we fixed the radiator leak before rivalry weekend. Hummer nailed Michigan over UCLA last week, and I won with Tennessee beating LSU . I vowed to never pick Lane Kiffin again this season as a betting favorite, and it worked out for me. I'm going to need a near-perfect showing to get back to even before bowl season. Let's hope it happens. TCU at No. 11 Texas Tech (-12.5) Hummer ( Texas Tech -12.5) : You never really know how a team is going to respond following its head coach's firing. But all I know going into this one is Texas Tech is playing for everything and TCU is playing for very little. So, I lean the Red Raiders here. As for the margin … TCU's defensive front is good enough to slow Texas Tech's run game. But I also have a very hard time seeing TCU's stuck-in-the-mud offense (100th nationally in yards per play) working all that well against a Texas Tech defense that seems to have found some form the last two weeks. … Texas Tech 34, TCU 20. Crawford (Texas Tech -12.5) : This one sets up for a Texas Tech blowout as long as the Horned Frogs fail to rally under an interim coach following the firing of Sonny Dykes this week. TCU has won five of the last six in the series, but that was prior to Texas Tech's rise in the NIL era, with a roster vastly superior to most Big 12 opponents. Tommy Castellanos had his first multi-turnover game with the Red Raiders last week, so look for him to be more protective of the football en route to the program's second straight Big 12 title game appearance. ... Texas Tech 31, TCU 14. No. 25 Nebraska at No. 13 Iowa (-4.5) Hummer ( Nebraska +4.5) : These are pretty similar teams. Two top 20 squads that are at their best running the ball and when their up-and-down QBs play clean. The difference is Iowa is a bit better up front, and Nebraska's QB, Anthony Colandrea , comes with a slightly higher ceiling. I like the way Nebraska is playing of late, and I think the against-the-spread value is with the Huskers. But I also believe Iowa is the better team and far more likely to execute down the stretch in a close game. Iowa eeks by to reach 10-2. … Iowa 20, Nebraska 17. Crawford (Nebraska +4.5) : Can Huskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea make enough plays outside of the pocket to keep drives alive and convert in the red zone this weekend? That will make the difference in this one. Nebraska may even find some success on the ground with Jamal Rule , who hasn't scored since Week 3 but leads the team in rushing this season with 5.3 yards per carry. When stakes are high in rivalry games, both teams usually play to their maximum standard, and it comes down to the end. That's where I'm going here. ... Iowa 20, Nebraska 16. No. 20 Florida (-5.5) at Florida State Hummer ( Florida -5.5) : Florida should roll in this game. The Seminoles are 2-1 since firing Mike Norvell, but the offense has struggled, and they were also just blown out, 28-10, by NC State . But … all the advanced data says that this will be a very close game. Like within a point or two. I just don't see that. The Seminoles are super injured, don't have much to play for and are going up against a Gators team with a better overall roster. Give me the Gators to cover. … Florida 27, Florida State 20. Crawford (Florida -5.5) : Did the Seminoles get caught looking ahead to rivalry weekend last week? I was stunned to flip the channel and see NC State with a double-digit lead in the second half at Doak Campbell. That was an embarrassing loss, one that might keep this team out of the postseason unless they find a way to beat the Gators. I don't see it happening if Florida finds some semblance of consistency defensively and gets a few stops early in the matchup. ... Florida 26, Florida State 17. No. 3 Texas (-10.5) at Texas A&M Hummer (Texas -10.5) : Have you seen the Texas A&M offense recently? The Aggies haven't hit double digits in a game since October, and it's not going to get any easier against a top-10 Texas defense. It's a rivalry game. The Aggies will play hard. But this shouldn't be close. The Longhorns win their third straight in this series. … Texas 28, Texas A&M 10. Crawford (Texas -10.5) : Will Muschamp be licking his chops here? His uber-talented defense against a quarterback making his second start? Takeaways should fall into the Longhorns' lap in a game they need to win to stay in the first-round home game conversation in the CFP. They may even get a matchup with Georgia in the SEC Championship Game to further boost the resume. The Aggies have scored two total touchdowns in their last three SEC games. I'd be surprised if they get one on Saturday. ... Texas 24, Texas A&M 6. No. 19 Louisville (-2.5) at Kentucky Hummer ( Louisville -2.5) : That may feel like a strange line given Kentucky 's start to the season. But the Cardinals, winners of seven straight games, are playing excellent football right now. They've got one of the most explosive offenses in college football (fifth nationally in yards per play) and a rushing defense (34th nationally) that's gotten much better throughout the year. Kentucky, on the other hand, has scored an average of just 11.3 points per game over the last three weeks. The Wildcats do have an advantage along the line of scrimmage. But the Cardinals are also just playing better. Give me the hot team. … Louisville 28, Kentucky 24. Crawford (Kentucky +2.5) : I understand why this one's tilted in Louisville's favor by oddsmakers. Kentucky's frail with three straight losses, but this one feels different for Will Stein in his first rival setting with the Wildcats. They're going all-in this week to salvage what's been a better-than-expected campaign in Lexington, and a victory over Louisville should push Kentucky to a Florida-based bowl game. After playing three straight challenging SEC defenses, Kenny Minchey gets a break against an opponent that ranks 10th in the ACC in total yards allowed. ... Kentucky 28, Louisville 27. Michigan at No. 21 Ohio State (-10.5) Hummer (Ohio State -10.5) : This is the first Michigan-Ohio State matchup since 2017 without any real national title or playoff implications. But there's plenty of pressure on both coaches. Kyle Whittingham remains very much on the hot seat. Ryan Day is amid the worst season of his Ohio State coaching career. I think the Buckeyes win. They're the better overall team. But it's going to be ugly. The defenses make plenty of plays. There is some bad offensive football from Michigan. The Buckeyes pull away late. … Ohio State 27, Michigan 10. Crawford (Michigan +10.5) : Admittedly, I have little confidence here that Michigan can generate enough positive plays to eventually get into scoring position against the Buckeyes. However, I know this defense will do everything in its power to keep Michigan in the game and make this one a late sweat for the home team. It's almost unimaginable that Ryan Day could lose five games as the former preseason No. 1 this fall. There's far too much talent on this Ohio State team to be stumbling down the stretch like this regardless of who's playing quarterback. ... Ohio State 17, Michigan 12. South Carolina (-4.5) at Clemson Hummer ( Clemson +4.5) : I'm not sure which one of these fan bases is all that happy entering this one. The Gamecocks have stalled down the stretch. Clemson is as far removed from the national title picture as it has been in 15 years. This is a game South Carolina should win. The Gamecocks are better. Better QB. Better offensive weapons. Comparable defense. But this is also exactly the type of game Clemson gets up for. picks.blurb: Week 13 College Football Predictions: College Football Picks for Rivalry Week, including USC vs UCLA Opens in a new tab Sportsnaut NFL NFL Schedule NFL Standings NFL Power Rankings NFL Defense Rankings NFL Offense Rankings NFL QB Rankings MLB MLB Power Rankings MLB Standings NBA NBA Playoffs Bracket NBA Power Rankings 50 Best NBA Players NHL NHL Standings NHL Power Rankings NASCAR NASCAR Standings NASCAR Power Rankings UFC Men's Pound for Pound Rankings Women's Pound for Pound Rankings COLLEGE College Basketball College Football Other College Sports High School Sports Add Sportsnaut on Google Add on Google Facebook The 2026 college football regular season draws to a close this weekend with Rivalry Week. Much of the chaos and surprises from throughout the fall have slightly diminished some of the matchups for things like The Game and the Egg Bowl, but it’s still worth making college football picks this weekend for a slate of games that mean so much to these programs. Let’s dive into our Week 13 college football picks this weekend for the top rivalry matchups. Ole Miss Rebels 38, Mississippi State Bulldogs 17 The Ole Miss Rebels are out of College Football Playoff contention, and the Mississippi State Bulldogs have been in a free fall since the 4-0 start to the season. While there aren’t major stakes for the Egg Bowl, this in-state battle still features two teams and fan bases that very much hate one another. Unfortunately for the Bulldogs, this offense hasn’t been the same since Kamario Taylor’s season-ending injury. In the last five games against SEC opponents, Mississippi State is averaging just 10 PPG with single-digit points against LSU, Texas and Auburn. Defensively, things have been nearly just as bad. In what could be his final start as the Rebels’ quarterback, Trinidad Chambliss will clear 300 total yards with four touchdowns and win the Egg Bowl for the second consecutive year. Iowa Hawkeyes 20, Nebraska Cornhuskers 14 The Iowa Hawkeyes steamrolled through the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Black Friday last season, with Kamari Moulton and Mark Gronowski combining for four rushing touchdowns and taking full advantage of their rival having no semblance of a passing game. Fast forward to 2026, Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule now has a viable threat in Anthony Colandrea, with his big-play ability proving instrumental in the win last week at Ohio State. Here’s the issue for Nebraska. Iowa boasts the second-best red zone defense (67.9% scoring rate) in the nation this season, and it ranks 11th among Power Four defenses in yards per play allowed (4.6). The Cornhuskers offense is inconsistent, as evidenced by a four-game stretch from Oct. 10 through Nov. 6 when it averaged just 13.5 PPG. This will be a much closer game than what took place last year, but the Hawkeyes’ defense and run game will pave the way to a win at home. Texas Longhorns 21, Texas A&M Aggies 7 Arch Manning is coming off one of his sharpest performances of the season, and he’s completed at least 73% of his passes with three-plus total touchdowns in three of his last four games. He does, however, still have a penchant for making poor decisions under pressure, and Mike Elko’s defense can get after the quarterback. Unfortunately for the Texas A&M Aggies, they have one of the worst offenses in the Power Four. This is a matchup ripe with opportunities for the Texas Longhorns defense to record four-plus sacks and multiple takeaways, regardless of who the Aggies’ starting quarterback in Week 13 is. As long as Manning doesn’t turn it over three times, Texas will win this one comfortably at Kyle Field. Ohio State Buckeyes 13, Michigan Wolverines 10 Neither the Ohio State Buckeyes nor the Michigan Wolverines are ranked entering The Game, a scenario that seemed unfathomable before the season kicked off. Michigan’s defense has been one of its few bright spots this season, and it should be able to take advantage of a leaky Buckeyes offensive line, limiting how many opportunities Luke Fahey has to target Jeremiah Smith downfield. The Wolverines also have some momentum coming into this one, with freshman running back Savion Hiter (108 scrimmage yards) and edge rusher John Henry Daley (two sacks) having just led them to an upset win over UCLA. However, Ohio State’s lone strength defensively this season has been its ability to stop the run (3.2 ypc and 100.3 rushing yards per game allowed). This is going to be an ugly football game, and there’s a path to Michigan embarrassing Ryan Day at home if Bryce Underwood can take advantage of facing an ineffective Buckeyes pass rush or the Wolverines let him and Hiter run wild with the RPO. Ohio State is favored here, and both teams figure to rely heavily on the run game. Ultimately, we think both the home-field advantage and the very different tone being set for The Game by both coaches leads to the Buckeyes pulling out an ugly one. Plus, one team has Smith and the other doesn’t. Louisville Cardinals 27, Kentucky Wildcats 24 The Louisville Cardinals and Kentucky Wildcats find themselves in two very different places coming into Week 13. Kentucky was in the top 10 of the College Football Playoff Rankings back in the first week of November, and it’s now lost three consecutive games, with two of those by double digits. Meanwhile, Louisville has clawed its way back from a 2-3 record after losing at NC State with a six-game winning streak, albeit those wins have come against some very bad competition. One thing we’re keeping an eye on: the Wildcats defense has allowed the ninth-highest passer rating (174.4) and yards per attempt ( 9.5 ) in college football over the last three weeks. Meanwhile, Louisville’s Lincoln Kienholz is coming off a five-touchdown performance, and this is a chance for him to potentially boost his stock further before shopping himself around to quarterback-needy programs this offseason. We just see a Kentucky program that is spiraling out of control under first-year head coach Will Stein, and there’s a lack of confidence in him salvaging it against Jeff Brohm’s Cardinals. Momentum, head-coaching experience and the better quarterback allow Louisville to win on the road. USC Trojans 20, UCLA Bruins 13 The UCLA Bruins aren’t ruling out quarterback Ty Dieffenbach playing on Saturday against the USC Trojans. We’re just not buying it and tend to believe it’s a bit of gamesmanship by head coach Bob Chesney. That would mean the Bruins are forced into starting Madden Iamaleava, who looked like one of the worst quarterbacks in college football coming in for relief against Michigan. UCLA still has a chance in this one because its defense has been spectacular throughout the season, allowing the lowest yards-per-play average (4.0), the sixth-lowest conversion rate on third down (29.22%) and the seventh-fewest red zone opportunities per game (2.5). With that said, running back Wayne Knight’s performance has plummeted in recent weeks. Against Wisconsin, Michigan State, Nevada, Illinois and Michigan, he totaled just 218 rushing yards (43.6 per game) and averaged only 3.2 yards per carry. While UCLA has the better head coach, its issues at quarterback and the sudden inability to run the football as effectively as they did earlier in the season will be its downfall against Lincoln Riley and Jayden Maiava. Oregon Ducks 34, Washington Huskies 24 Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola is on a hot streak right now, coming into this game with 1,168 passing yards (292 pass ypg), a 10-0 TD-INT line and a 66.2% completion rate in the last four games. We are not, however, buying into this two-game stretch from the Ducks defense and firmly believe this side of the ball is what opens the door to the Washington Huskies potentially pulling off the upset on Saturday night. With this game being played in Eugene and Dan Lanning’s program having a shot to earn a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game, we do think the Ducks will come out highly motivated for this one and deliver their fourth consecutive win by double-digit points. Alabama Crimson Tide 28, Auburn Tigers 14 We can’t wait to see how the College Football Playoff committee turns this into another incredible victory for the Alabama Crimson Tide. The Auburn Tigers did win at Georgia back on Oct. 17, with quarterback Byrum Brown torching them on the ground for 115 yards. Brown has also done a much better job of protecting the football in the second half of the season, throwing just one interception on 149 pass attempts after having seven picks in his first five games. Alabama’s defense is, however, very good at both creating takeaways and forcing athletic quarterbacks to beat them from the pocket. The Crimson Tide will generate two takeaways in the Iron Bowl, and a three-touchdown performance by Keelon Russell will propel this team to victory. Got a story or tip for us? picks.headline: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri
picks.blurb: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Aaron Rodgers benched Latest CFP rankings MLB free agency updates NBA Cup roundup Viral Ga. Tech couple Corbie Craig Contributing writer Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College football rivalry week is here, and some of the toughest teams to price are the ones making changes this late in the season. Oklahoma has won three straight with Jason Witten calling plays, Minnesota just won after changing its offensive coordinator, and Wisconsin got a big performance from a quarterback who had lost his starting job. There are reasons to believe those offenses are improving, but I want to be careful about how much of last Saturday carries into this week. I'm starting with three unders, looking at the way these teams have been moving the ball and how much work it takes them to score. Here are my three early Week 13 bets. No. 19 Oklahoma at No. 24 Missouri (-1.5, 41.5) Oklahoma has looked better since Witten took over. Quarterback John Mateer has settled down, and the offense is giving its defense a chance to rest. I understand why people would expect more points here. Against Ole Miss, all three of Oklahoma's offensive scoring drives took at least 12 plays, and Isaiah Sategna added a punt-return touchdown, which helped turn a game in which Mateer threw for 111 yards into a 24-17 win. Then against Texas A&M, the Sooners were tied entering the fourth quarter before finishing a 15-play touchdown drive that took more than eight minutes. A later interception set up a one-play touchdown to Sategna, making the final score look a lot more comfortable than the game had been. Witten can keep Mateer in manageable situations, use the running game and keep Missouri's offense off the field. Oklahoma's defense has held Florida and Texas A&M to seven points apiece during this stretch, with Ole Miss scoring 17 between them. Missouri will test it. QB Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes against Kentucky, and WR Donovan Olugbode caught two of them. I'm more concerned about those receivers creating quick scores than Missouri consistently driving the length of the field. The Tigers also allowed Kentucky into the red zone seven times while giving up only 14 points, so their defense gave up more chances than the final score suggests. I expect Oklahoma to stick with the patient approach that has worked under Witten, while making Simmons put together longer drives to score. Bet: Under 41.5 (-110) Minnesota at Wisconsin (-7.5, 37.5) Wisconsin just scored 42 points at Purdue, so this is a pretty low number to come back and bet under. RB Colton Joseph returned to the starting job and ran for 187 yards, including touchdowns from 32 and 66 yards out. Darrion Dupree broke a long touchdown run, too. Purdue couldn't handle the quarterback run game, and Wisconsin kept going back to it. Minnesota has to do a better job there. The Gophers allowed Northwestern to rush for 196 yards, and Joseph gave Wisconsin a way to turn a missed assignment into a touchdown without throwing the ball. That's the biggest concern with this bet — but I still don't trust Minnesota to score much. P.J. Fleck fired offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. after the Penn State loss, and Eric Koehler took over the play-calling against Northwestern. Darius Taylor ran the ball better and two missed field goals hurt, but the Gophers still went into halftime scoreless. Their first touchdown required a fourth-down conversion, and Anthony Smith then forced and recovered a fumble to give Minnesota a short field for its second TD. QB Drake Lindsey made a great throw late to set up the winning field goal, but even with those plays, Minnesota finished with only 20 points. It hasn't scored more than that in any of its past six games. I can give the coaching change some credit without expecting everything to be fixed before a trip to Wisconsin. The Badgers' defense ranks No. 21 in our ratings, and neither offense is in much of a hurry between snaps. If Minnesota can make Joseph and Dupree string together first downs instead of breaking long runs, Wisconsin can move the ball while taking plenty of time off the clock. Bet: Under 37.5 (-110) North Dakota State (-9.5, 39.5) at San José State San José State nearly forced overtime against UNLV, but the offense still had to work awfully hard to get to 22 points. QB Luke Weaver threw 40 passes while the Spartans ran for just 56 yards. They needed a late touchdown pass to Carson Clark to get within a 2-point conversion then couldn't complete the tying attempt. A week earlier, they scored three points at Air Force. We still rank this offense 128th, and I'm not convinced Weaver gets enough help from the running game to keep it moving against North Dakota State. The Bison's defense certainly gave us a reason to hesitate last week. They led Northern Illinois 31-3 before allowing touchdowns on the Huskies' final three possessions. I still put more weight on a defense we rank No. 29, which held Hawai'i to 13 points and UTEP to seven in its previous two games. San José State needs to sustain drives against that group, and its past two games haven't given me much confidence it can. QB Nathan Hayes is coming off a career-high four touchdown passes, but the Bison finished Saturday by adding defensive tackles as blockers and handing the ball to DJ Scott to run out the clock. With North Dakota State favored here, I expect it to lean on the running game if it gets ahead. I'll back its defense to keep San José State from turning this into a game Hayes has to win through the air. Bet: Under 39.5 (+100)
