Now the old Big Eight foes meet in Columbia with both teams at 7-4, and I think the market has the wrong team laying points. Jason Witten's offense isn't pretty, and that's the point After Ben Arbuckle was let go, Jason Witten took over as interim offensive coordinator, and the offense has leaned hard into ball control. Against No. 19 Ole Miss in rain and wind, Oklahoma ran it 49 times for 188 yards and put together four drives of 12 plays or more. Last week John Mateer threw for 269 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another in a 28-7 win over Texas A&M, his third straight game with at least 56 rushing yards under Witten. “There's something to be said about not flinching at that position, and everybody kind of follows your lead,” Witten said of his quarterback. The Sooners aren't trying to win 38-35. They're trying to keep the ball, flip the field, and let the defense finish the job. For the season, Oklahoma gives up 17.9 points per game and just 163.1 passing yards per game, which CollegeFFB's opponent-adjusted numbers rate among the ten best pass defenses in the country. Copy Link copied Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables discusses the challenges Missouri presents on both sides of the ball as the Sooners prepare for their regular-season finale in Columbia. Oklahoma will look to extend its winning streak to four games and finish the regular season with eight wins when the Sooners travel to Missouri on Saturday. Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables said Tuesday that the Tigers present a significant challenge on both sides of the ball, particularly given their ability to protect the football and their success at home this season. Missouri is 5-1 at home and leads the SEC in turnover margin. Venables praised Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons for his decision-making and efficiency, noting that Simmons has thrown for more than 2,500 yards with just four interceptions this season. The Tigers also feature running back Jamal Roberts, who has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards this season, and a receiving corps that has helped Missouri become more explosive offensively. Venables said limiting big plays, tackling well and maintaining discipline will be important for Oklahoma’s defense against Missouri’s balanced offense. He also credited Missouri’s defensive front and the team’s fundamentals under head coach Eli Drinkwitz. “This is a team that’s gonna force you to play very clean fundamentally,” Venables said. The Sooners (7-4, 5-3 SEC) enter Saturday’s matchup having won three consecutive games, including a 28-7 victory over Texas A&M in their final home game of the season. Oklahoma’s offensive improvement during that stretch has come under interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten. Venables praised Witten’s work but declined to provide a timeline for naming a permanent offensive coordinator. “Jason’s done a fantastic job. That goes without saying,” Venables said. “You guys will find out soon enough.” Venables said Witten has provided clear direction for the offensive coaching staff and helped establish expectations following the midseason change. He also credited improved health, offensive balance and the team’s ability to sustain drives for its recent success. Quarterback John Mateer has played a significant role in Oklahoma’s late-season turnaround, accounting for all four touchdowns in Saturday’s victory over Texas A&M. Venables praised Mateer’s response to criticism and setbacks throughout his time at Oklahoma, pointing to his maturity and willingness to take responsibility. “He’s hung in there, and he’s made the best of it, and I’m proud of him,” Venables said. Looking ahead to next season, Venables said quarterbacks Whit Newbauer and Bo Bentley have benefited from additional practice repetitions while the coaching staff has managed Mateer’s workload. He said there is an opportunity for either young quarterback to compete for the starting job next season. With early signing day approaching, Venables also expressed optimism about Oklahoma’s player retention efforts, saying several players have indicated they intend to return next season. He said the Sooners have a promising foundation along the offensive line, with six high school players expected to join the program and additional opportunities to address depth through the transfer portal. As Oklahoma prepares for its final regular-season game, Venables said he is thankful for the way his players have continued to respond throughout the season. The Sooners will travel to Columbia on Saturday looking to carry their late-season momentum into the postseason. away.blurb: A total of eight players appeared on Indiana's Week 12 availability report on Thursday night. Six of those players have already been ruled out for Saturday's contest against the Huskies, and that group includes some key starters. The biggest losses for Indiana come on the offensive side of the ball. RB Turbo Richard and OL Joe Brunner both being unavailable for the second straight week is a tough blow to Indiana's rushing attack. After taking down USC by a score of 27-13 last week, the Indiana Hoosiers are hitting the road in Week 12. Traveling across the country to Seattle, this weekend's tilt against Washington is the furthest road trip of the regular season for IU. For the most part, Indiana has stayed relatively healthy this season. Curt Cignetti has a solid strategy in place to keep his players healthy, which includes prioritizing player recovery, managing practice workloads, and ensuring athletes receive proper rest and conditioning throughout the season. But at the end of the day, this is still football and injuries happen. Heading into Week 12, the Hoosiers are dealing with some injuries to key players that present some challenges against Washington. Indiana Football Week 12 injury report Here's a look at the full availability report for Indiana heading into Week 12: Richard was brought in from Boston College over the offseason to be Indiana's RB1, and he thrived in that role when healthy. Richard has rushed for 745 yards and team-leading 6.6 yards per carry with 6 touchdowns this season. The good news is that Khobie Martin is back after missing the first half of the season with a broken forearm, and he rushed 12 times for 82 yards and a touchdown last week against USC. Lee Beebe Jr. has also been a reliable rushing force this season, and he totaled 71 yards on 16 carries last week against the Trojans. With Richard sidelined, Martin and Beebe figure to share the workload in the Hoosier backfield once again. Brunner is a fifth-year senior who has been a key part of Indiana's offensive line this season. He transferred to Indiana from Wisconsin back in the spring, and brought plenty of experience with him as he appeared in 39 games with 24 starts during his career with the Badgers. Owning a 6'7" 320-pound frame, Brunner started the first nine games of the season at right guard for the Hoosiers. In his absence, redshirt sophomore Austin Liebfried got the starting nod at right guard against USC on Saturday afternoon. He could be expected to continue in that role, but freshman Sam Simpson could also see expanded opportunities. Last week without Richard and Brunner, Indiana ran for 146 yards and 4.2 yards per carry against USC. Washington's run defense isn't the best in the world, as the Huskies rank 10th in the Big Ten by allowing 132.4 rushing yards per game to their opponents. away.headline: Indiana football's overtime loss at Washington makes CFP a long shot | Overreactions
away.blurb: This might be an overreaction, but one suspects Curt Cignetti wouldn't see it as such. Cignetti directly called out his defense this week for its problems against mobile quarterbacks, only for his words to turn prophetic when Demond Williams Jr. scrambled for a 65-yard touchdown on Washington's opening drive. Replays suggested Williams might have stepped out of bounds, but the moment was no aberration. We've wondered for months what kind of depth Indiana had along an offensive line that's very young behind its preferred first five. For better or worse, the Hoosiers were forced to find out Saturday. We wondered whether the Hoosiers would need Hoover again this season. The answer always felt like yes. And it turned out, it was. SEATTLE — Indiana football couldn't help itself in an overtime loss at Washington on Saturday. The Hoosiers ' path to the Big Ten championship game, and perhaps College Football Playoff, became more difficult after a 27-24 loss to the Huskies . A change at quarterback, Josh Hoover relieving starter Grant Wilson, was effective. However the change from Nico Radicic to Paddy McAteer was negligible. Radicic had a kick blocked, which was followed by the change. McAteer made a field goal in regulation but missed in overtime. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. That was Indiana 's worst defensive half of the season In total, Indiana allowed 264 total yards of offense in the opening two quarters, with nine explosive plays allowed and three personal foul penalties (all of them on Williams; two roughing, one late hit). Washington averaged more than 7 yards per play. Preston Zachman's interception in the end zone kept it from getting worse, and underscored Zachman's escalating importance to this defense. But that did not color over all that went wrong from a unit we've come to expect as much more capable than it looked in the first half Saturday in Seattle. Offensive line injuries might drown IU's offense Time will tell if this is an overreaction. It's certainly testing the Hoosiers' depth, at least. After losing right guard Joe Brunner to a non-contact ACL injury in practice late last week, the Hoosiers had to adjust without center Bray Lynch for the second half Saturday, after Lynch was rolled up from behind and had to be helped off into the injury tent on a stuffed run on fourth down near midfield. Austin Leibfried, who took over for Brunner last week against Southern Cal, slid one spot to the left and took Lynch's center spot in the second half. Baylor Wilkin stepped in at right guard. What we know: Indiana starting center injured at Washington Hoosiers needed Josh Hoover again And he delivered. When Grant Wilson began to struggle, Indiana turned back to Josh Hoover, and he gave his team shot in the arm to the tune of multiple scoring drives in the second half. None more important than the shot he took to Nick Marsh for a 35-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter. More: Curt Cignet
